feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: International news, global reporting and analysis from NPR. Plus dispatches from NPR’s State of the World podcast.

entry.title: Democrats win House by largest margin in 50 years. And, COP31 ends with no deal
entry.summary: Democrats have currently flipped 47 House seats and could flip 49 total. And, climate change talks at COP31 ran two days longer than expected, becoming the longest conference in the summit's history.

entry.title: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya
entry.summary: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault.

entry.title: Ukraine war spilling into NATO territory
entry.summary: The war between Russia and Ukraine once again creeps onto European territory – from attacks on ships to missiles in Poland and fresh allegations of Russian operations inside Denmark.

entry.title: Luxury development planned on land some Albanians say is theirs, not Jared Kushner's
entry.summary: A company working for President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner purchased 300 acres of Albanian land for more than $130 million in April. But Albanians in the area tell NPR this is not Kushner's land -- it's theirs.

entry.title: Lebanese villagers return to wrecked homes as the Israeli army pulls back
entry.summary: In a pilot project in a village in southern Lebanon, Israeli forces have left and the Lebanese army moved it. But villagers who return find their houses wrecked.

entry.title: Climate change talks fall apart in final hours over fossil fuels
entry.summary: Some 200 countries gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the annual climate negotiations. Countries failed to reach an agreement over fossil fuels - the primary driver of global warming.

entry.title: What did Xi Jinping get from the bear hug with Trump at the Shenzhen summit?
entry.summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Robert Daly, director of the program on US China relations at University of Maryland's School of Public Policy, about President Trump's trip to China this week.

entry.title: Highlights and challenges from covering an historic month in South America
entry.summary: NPR's South America Correspondent discusses her work covering an historic election upset and a papal visit.

entry.title: A grieving family in Lebanon returns to their village
entry.summary: In Southern Lebanon, the Army is taking over after Israeli forces withdraw. One grieving family returns to their village to find almost everything in their house destroyed.

entry.title: Cartel leader captured in northern Mexico in a bloody firefight that left 11 dead
entry.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, better known as "El Chapo Isidro," was one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives. His arrest in northwest Mexico on Saturday has sparked violence in the region.
